title: [Lean] Recover binary certificates from named JSON and original bytes
body:
## Coverage and checked context

Explicit author-checked kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000 = 0.001672660197076918, at upstream main 0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea. These generic components do not change that exponent.

Four unchanged checked modules recover a permutation/inverse and binary chart certificate from packed columns plus update/form vectors, connect it to an actual named JSON field, and connect both calls/owners and recovery to original byte arrays.

Finite coverage: arbitrary finite dimensions including zero; recovery completeness is restricted to one involutive rank-one update after a coordinate permutation. Arbitrary invertibility is insufficient, and no efficient uniform recovery cost is asserted.

Conditional-interface coverage: successful byte execution exposes the installed UTF-8/JSON parser equations, exact named-field AST, independent column operator and both inverse laws. Auxiliary certificate data are generated internally. Parser standards, lexical/duplicate-key policy, actual selected-file success, key/digest provenance and update/form provenance remain explicit obligations.

Full-theorem coverage: this does not supply complex phases, affine shifts, physical execution/allocation/direction, precision, recursive cost accounting or the all-size multiplication/runtime theorem.

## Validation and reproduction

Four new sources total 30,860 bytes. Fifteen standard-only axiom probes and seven complete printed theorem types passed local kernel checks and independent exact-source/terminal review. The public manifest binds unchanged source hashes and observed evidence. Lean 4.21.0 and Mathlib 308445d7985027f538e281e18df29ca16ede2ba3 are pinned.

REPRODUCTION.md describes a fresh isolated serial 17-module source closure. It was inspected, not executed again for publication. No extra local CI preflight was run. Thin selected L450 applications and canonical owner exports are excluded.

## Dependencies, overlap and credit

Thirteen unchanged prerequisites are reused by immutable reference, without copying: PR #1831 at 542f914ca0e5df4026341d08c84385cb1a71cfdf; PR #1879 at 981afe759f7dd206188b1c1a62250c6425bcd76a; PR #1927 at a5838afac3a2d69d802c2440cbfa7d160ca0b218. Compared with those parser/chart/JSON adapters, the new work generates the restricted certificate from actual columns and supplies byte-entrypoint composition. No broad novelty claim is made.

Credit: Lean/Mathlib authors; Jeremy Kothe T16/PR514 and PR484/507 lineage; Rohan Arun PR1094; predecessor strict-parser, permutation, gather and chart work. James Chang with OpenAI assistance; Apache-2.0. Existing source comments and attribution are preserved.

Next useful obligation: connect exact compact column fragments to the decoded named field, while retaining parser and provenance limits explicitly.
